definitions.explanation: A snack of thin biscuit sticks dipped in chocolate, with a bare end to hold, made by Ezaki Glico since 1966. One of the best-known Japanese sweets, sold in many flavors.

examples.japanese: ポッキー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ポッキー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{分|わ}けた→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧。
examples.english: I shared some Pocky with a friend.

examples.japanese: {十一月十一日|じゅういちがつじゅういちにち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ポッキー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいた→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: November 11 is Pocky Day, so the convenience store had piles of them on display.

notes:
The name imitates the snapping sound ぽきっ of a breaking stick. Counted with {本|ほん} (one stick) or ⟦{箱|はこ}→箱：02162_hako⟧ (one box).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ポッキー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: Pocky Day, November 11 (the date 11/11 looks like four sticks)
- ポッキー⟦ゲーム→ゲーム：03842_geemu⟧: a party game in which two people eat one stick from both ends
- ポッキー⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧: one stick of Pocky
